Maria (Partnerships): Quick heads-up — our HW partner flagged a perf regression after driver 535.98 + CUDA 12.3 on their nvidia-c9 instances, and one SI is blocked for marketplace onboarding. Can we triage?
AJ (Eng-runtime): Thanks — I'm on it. Can you attach the partner logs or ticket id?
Maria (Partnerships): Ticket #PRT-4821 from Vendor (link: https://vendor.example/t/PRT-4821). They included perf numbers and a flamegraph.
AJ (Eng-runtime): Reproduced on a local repro VM. Running inference with our standard benchmark shows median p50 latency jump from 120ms -> 270ms for batch=8.
AJ (Eng-runtime): Repro command I used:
```bash
python bench/infer_bench.py --model redwood-3b --batch 8 --seq 2048 --cuda 12.3
```
Lia (Ops): Do we know if it's the driver or CUDA runtime? Any segfaults?
AJ (Eng-runtime): No OOMs or segfaults, just increased kernel times. nvprof sample shows longer convolution kernel times and more PCIe stalls. Looks driver-related.
Sam (Platform): Marketplace images currently pin drivers to 535.98 per our recent policy. If this is driver-induced regression we may need a short-term pin override for affected SKUs.
Ken (Marketplace): We need an action that doesn't block the SI onboarding. Options: 1) temporarily mark affected SKUs as "unsupported" in the marketplace listing, 2) push a marketplace-only driver patch that bundles a vendor-approved driver, or 3) coordinate an immediate hotfix with the HW partner. Thoughts?
Maria (Partnerships): Partner is willing to try a backported micro-fix but wants our help verifying. They can build a candidate driver (535.99-candidate).
AJ (Eng-runtime): I can validate 535.99-candidate in our internal CI farm. Need a deterministic test plan to run across the SKU matrix and the repro harness.
Lia (Ops): Suggestion: run a canary on two instance types (nvidia-c9, nvidia-p4x) in us-west-2, 50 requests/sec for 30m, compare latency/err rates vs baseline. If green, we schedule gradual rollout and update marketplace pin. If not, rollback.
Ken (Marketplace): I can update listing metadata to add a note and a short-term SKU exclusion. Also can add a short-form "compatibility advisory" on the marketplace page so the SI knows why onboarding is delayed.
driver-bot: Created internal ticket RDW-6123: "Validate vendor driver 535.99-candidate across marketplace SKUs" (<https://redwood.internal/t/RDW-6123>)
AJ (Eng-runtime): Plan: I will run the benchmark matrix tonight and post a summary in this thread. If 535.99 looks good, we coordinate with Ken to unpin/pin marketplace images, and Maria to handshake partner announcement.
Maria (Partnerships): Timeline note — partner wants a joint statement only after sign-off. We should avoid public mentions until we confirm.
Lia (Ops): Add rollback playbook now: revert to driver 534.xx image, revert marketplace SKU flag, and open immediate pager if error rate > 5% during rollout window.
Sam (Platform): I'll prepare the images and a short script to flip the pin via infra API (example below):
```python
# flip-driver-pin.py
import requests
requests.post('https://infra.api/pins', json={"sku":"nvidia-c9","driver":"535.99-candidate"})
```
Ken (Marketplace): Cool. Once AJ posts results, I can schedule the listing update. Maria, please coordinate partner NDA/legal signoff if we include their name in any advisory.
Maria (Partnerships): Will do. Thanks everyone.
AJ (Eng-runtime): Posting first pass numbers in ~4hrs.
Ken (Marketplace): Marking this thread for follow-up in tomorrow's standup. :white_check_mark:
Lia (Ops): Adding test run to the nightly canary queue now.
Maria (Partnerships): thanks all :pray: — trying to keep SI on the lane for dev integration, will update when partner replies.
driver-bot: RDW-6123 status updated -> in-progress
